statements.claim: Krishna came to Vidarbha as a guest, having slain Kamsa but not taken the throne of Mathura, with no city, crown, or seat among the kings at Kundina for the swayamvara.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: Krishna arrived at the city of Vidarbha with Vinata's son 'as our guest'; Janamejaya: 'having slain the highly powerful Kansa Krishna did not sit on the throne'; kings assembled 'in this city of Kundina for the maiden'.

statements.claim: Jarasandha's taunt: Devaki's son has never been installed and holds no city, so how shall he sit in the assembly of kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Devaki's son has not been installed on a throne and he has no city. How will he sit in the same assembly with the kings.'

statements.claim: Kratha and Kaishika, the brothers who ruled Vidarbha, thought that beholding Krishna's consecration would wash away their sins and that there is no worthier person in the three worlds.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Forsooth shall our sins be destroyed if we behold the wonderful Abhisheka of Krishna... there is no other worthier person in the three worlds'; 'the two heroic and noble kings of Vidarbha'.

statements.claim: The brothers bowed low and said: 'Blessed is our birth and our fame today; blessed are our ancestors, since you have come to our house.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Blessed is our birth and fame to-day; blessed are our ancestral manes since thou hast come to our house.'

statements.claim: They offered their umbrellas, flagstaffs, throne, army and flourishing city, reminded Krishna he was anointed by Indra as Upendra, and installed him in their kingdom, which no host of kings, not even Jarasandha, could undo.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'We ourselves, our umbrellas, flag-staffs, throne, army and our flourishing city belong to thee... formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra. We now install thee in our kingdom... The innumerable kings and even the Emperor Jarāsandha will not be able to undo what both of us will do.'

statements.claim: Bhishmaka, father of the maiden, seeing dissension brewing, prepared a fine resting house for Krishna after consulting the brothers.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'the king Bhishmaka, after consulting with us, has got ready this most excellent resting house' to stop dissension about seats; Bhishmaka is the father of the maiden for whose swayamvara the kings gathered.

statements.claim: The brothers urged Krishna to perform the royal unction that day and be installed next morning as emperor at the behest of Indra.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Having performed today the ceremony of royal unction... do thou, next morning, seated at ease on an auspicious throne... be installed as the Emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra.'

statements.claim: Kaishika told the assembly that his eldest brother Kratha had conferred the kingdom, and that when Kratha said 'Sit on this seat' an invisible speech was uttered by a sky-ranger.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'my eldest brother Kratha... has conferred upon Vasudeva his kingdom. When my brother said Sit on this seat an invisible speech was uttered by a sky-ranger.'

statements.claim: The celestial emissary announced a white seat of gold built by the celestial Architect, crested with gems and marked with a lion emblem, and that Krishna must not be offered a seat others had sat on.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'thou shouldst not offer to Vāsudeva the seat on which thou didst sit. For him the king of gods has sent this white seat of gold, constructed by the celestial Architect, crested with all sorts of jems and marked with an emblem of a lion.'

statements.claim: Whoever among the kings assembled for the maiden fails to come will be slain by the king of gods, and eight jars of celestial gold and jewels from the lord of riches will come to install the emperor.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'He, who amongst the kings assembled in this city of Kundina for the maiden will not come, will be slain by the king of gods. The eight jars, born of the portions of Nidhis made of celestial gold and jewels... will come amongst those kings for installing this Emperor.'

statements.claim: The emissary gave Krishna the seat, effulgent like the rising sun, and returned to the city of the gods.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'giving to Krishna, the seat, effulgent like the rising sun the celestial emissary returns to the city of gods.'

statements.claim: Witnessing the ceremony — the bathing of the God of gods — destroys sins.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'If we behold the wonderful ceremony, the bathing of Vishnu, the God of gods, surely our sins wi[ll be destroyed].'

notes: Story closely tracks Harivamsha 1.107, including direct dialogue. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Krishna was seated on the white seat of gold among the assembled kings, with the emissary of Indra having delivered his charge, for the royal unction.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: the white seat of gold 'marked with an emblem of a lion' was sent for Krishna; 'Do thou along with other kings place him on this seat and sprinkle him'; the Abhisheka was performed 'before the very presence of the kings'.

statements.claim: Celestial jars poured down from the sky like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders, over the seated Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107 excerpt: 'from the sky, celestial jars ... began to pour down, like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders on the occasion of the ceremony of his royal unction.'

statements.claim: The eight jars promised by the voice — born of the treasures of the lord of riches, of celestial gold studded with jewels, carrying celestial ornaments — came among the kings and joined the anointing.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'The eight jars, born of the portions of Nidhis made of celestial gold and jewels and containing celestial ornaments belonging to the high-souled lord of riches, will come amongst those kings for installing this Emperor.'

statements.claim: Indra, who had once anointed Krishna as Upendra, sprinkled him from the welkin, and the Abhisheka was performed duly according to rites before the presence of the kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra'; the king of gods 'will sprinkle him from the welkin with jars'; 'Having performed duly according to rites, the Abhisheka ceremony of Janārddana, before the very presence of the kings.'

statements.claim: Krishna was seated on the seat marked with the emblem of a lion, as emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'seat... marked with an emblem of a lion'; 'be installed as the Emperor of the kings assembled at the behest of Indra'.

statements.claim: Jarasandha had mocked Krishna as having no throne and no city; the consecration answered how he should sit among kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107: 'Devaki's son has not been installed on a throne and he has no city. How will he sit in the same assembly with the kings.'

notes: Story renders Harivamsha 1.107 consecration. 'Indra himself came down to finish what he had set in motion' is a mild physical dramatization of the pack-supported 'sprinkle him from the welkin' — treated as connective, no factual conflict.

statements.claim: Before leaving Vidarbha, Krishna told the assembled kings: 'I shall repair to the charming city of Mathura, governed by the Bhoja king.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'I shall repair to the charming city of Mathura governed by the Bhoja king.'

statements.claim: Garuda asked leave to examine Kushasthali at the base of Mount Raivata on the shore of the ocean — abandoned by rakshasas, rich with flowering trees and teeming with wild creatures — and set off toward the west.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'I shall now proceed to Raivata's city Kushasthali... The Rākshasas have abandoned the charming city... situated at the base of the Raivata mountain and on the bank of the great ocean. It abounds in trees decorated with filaments of flowers... inhabited by bear, monkeys, boars, buffaloes and deer... set out towards the western direction.'

statements.claim: Krishna, with the Yadavas, entered Mathura, where the news of his installation by numberless kings, Indra's peace made through his envoy Chitrangada, and the apportionment of wealth had already reached Ugrasena.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'when Krishna too, with the Yadavas, entered into the beautiful city of Mathurā'; 'Hearing of Krishna's installation as the Emperor by numberless kings, of Indra's making peace with him through his envoy Chitrangada, of the apportionment of wealth... every one, who came there, did not go away empty handed.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena offered a great puja at the temples of the tutelary deities, decorated Vasudeva's gate and Kamsa's assembly hall, anointed the doors of Krishna's sitting-room with sweet paste, and filled the city with music, flags, garlands, jars of water, sandal water on the roads, cloth on the ground and burning aguru incense.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'Ugrasena offered a great _puja_ at the temples of the tutelary deities... The doors of the sitting-room of the Emperor Krishna in Gopura were pasted with ambrosia... The city was decorated with flags, garlands of wild flowers and jars full of water. The king sprinkled sandal water in all the high-ways and spread sheets of cloth on the ground... incense was kept in vessels and continually burnt with Aguru.'

statements.claim: The elderly women sang benedictory hymns and young women moved about anxiously in their houses.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'The elderly women began to sing benedictory hymns and youthful damsels moved about anxiously in their respective houses.'

statements.claim: The conch Panchajanya sounded and the whole city came out — women, boys, elders, panegyrists, songsters and a huge army — with Balarama placed before them, while Ugrasena carried the arghya and water for washing Krishna's feet.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'the great sound of the conch-shell Pānchajanya was heard... the entire city of Mathurā... issued out placing Rāma before them. Ugrasena himself carried _arghya_ and water for washing feet for Krishna.'

statements.claim: Seeing Krishna seated on a car adorned with celestial jewels and a wild-flower garland, Ugrasena got down from his white car and said it did not behove him to proceed on a car.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112: 'seated on a charming car adorned with celestial jewels... the garland of wild flowers decorating his breast... got down from his white car'; 'it does not behove me to proceed on car after this... Do thou go on the car.'

statements.claim: Krishna declined the royal honors and told Ugrasena: 'while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise... get upon your white car and govern the city of Mathura delightedly, with your sons and grandsons.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.112 (excerpt): 'O king of Mathurā, while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise... get upon your white car... govern the city of Mathurā, delightedly with your sons and grand-sons.' The 'declined the royal arghya' rendering is the substance of this refusal speech.

statements.claim: Kamsa had seized the throne and imprisoned his father; Krishna had freed Ugrasena and would not take the seat from him.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21 (DKS_0126 pack): 'The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne.' Consistent with Krishna's refusal speech in Harivamsha 1.112.

notes: Story tracks Harivamsha 1.112 closely, including direct dialogue. 'Declined the royal arghya' is a faithful compression of the refusal speech. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Ugrasena sat on the throne of Mathura after Krishna freed him from confinement, and the funeral rites for Kamsa and the rest of the slain were performed.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne... performed the funeral rites of Kansa, and of the rest of the slain.'

statements.claim: Krishna stood before Ugrasena as a servant and said: 'command boldly what else is to be done.'
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Sovereign lord, command boldly what else is to be done.'

statements.claim: The curse of Yayati had pronounced the Yadava race unworthy of dominion; with Krishna as servant, Ugrasena could issue orders to the gods.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'The curse of Yayáti has pronounced our race unworthy of dominion but with me, for your servant, you may issue your orders to the gods. How should kings disobey them?'

statements.claim: Long ago Yayati's son Yadu refused to take his father's old age upon himself, and for that refusal his line was denied the right to rule.
statements.evidence: Canonical origin of the Yayati curse named in the pack (Vishnu Purana 5.21 references 'the curse of Yayáti'); the Yadu-refusal backstory is the standard account of that curse in the same tradition and is consistent with the pack.

statements.claim: Krishna sent Vayu to Indra to desire him to lay aside his pomp and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Go, Váyu, to Indra, and desire him to lay aside his pomp, and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman.'

statements.claim: Indra laid aside his pomp and immediately gave up the hall Sudharman, which thenceforth passed into the keeping of the Yadava chiefs.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.21: 'Indra... immediately gave up to him the hall Sudharman.' Pack summary: 'the Yadava chiefs thenceforth possess the jewel-adorned celestial court.'

statements.claim: Indra, who had once anointed Krishna as Upendra and sent the golden seat for his consecration, surrendered the hall without refusal.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.107 (DKS_0123/0124 packs): 'formerly thou wert annointed by Indra as Upendra' and the golden seat sent for Krishna's consecration; Vishnu Purana 5.21: Indra gave up the hall immediately.

statements.claim: The curse was not lifted: the Yadavas still could not claim the crown in their own right, but gathered under Sudharman as though they could.
statements.evidence: Interpretive gloss consistent with Vishnu Purana 5.21: the curse 'has pronounced our race unworthy of dominion' (unlifted), while the hall was given to Ugrasena.

notes: Tracks Vishnu Purana 5.21. The Yadu-refusal sentence is background for the pack-named curse, consistent with tradition — not flagged. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa had sent demons and foes against the boy of Vraja: Putana was drained of her life, the wagon overturned, the two arjuna trees shattered, Kaliya driven from the Yamuna, and Dhenuka, Pralamba and Arishta slain.
statements.evidence: Vishnu Purana 5.15: 'Arisht́a the bull-demon and Dhenuka and Pralamba had been slain, Govarddhana had been lifted up, the serpent Kálíya had been subdued, the two trees had been broken, the female fiend Pútaná had been killed, and the waggon had been overturned.'

statements.claim: Kamsa believed the child the prophecy warned of — Devaki's eighth son — was dead, and that he had killed the substitute infant years before in the prison.
statements.evidence: VP 5.15: Narada related 'the whole, beginning with the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá' — i.e., Kamsa had been deceived into believing the prophesied child dead; the substitute daughter was killed in his place (SB 10.36.16: the daughter of Yashoda exchanged for Krishna).

statements.claim: Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.15-18 (rendered): 'Narada came and told Kamsa that Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.'

statements.claim: On the night of his birth Vasudeva carried the newborn Krishna across the Yamuna in secret and left him with Nanda and Yashoda, taking their infant daughter back to the prison in his place.
statements.evidence: VP 5.15: 'the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá'; SB 10.36.16: 'yaśodāyāḥ sutāṃ kanyāṃ devakyāḥ kṛṣṇam eva ca' (the daughter of Yashoda, and Krishna the son of Devaki) — the exchange; the Yamuna crossing is part of the same canonical transference account.

statements.claim: The child Kamsa seized and dashed that night was Yashoda's daughter, not Devaki's son.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.16-17: the exchange of the daughter for Krishna; hearing of it, 'the lord of the Bhojas' was agitated with anger (kopāt pracalitendriyaḥ).

statements.claim: Balarama was the son of Rohini, hidden in Vraja all those years in the same way.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Krishna and Balarama were the sons of Devaki and Rohini, whom the frightened Vasudeva had entrusted to Nanda.'

statements.claim: Narada showed that these two were Kamsa's death, and Kamsa's senses shook with rage.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.17-18: 'kopāt pracalitendriyaḥ... nivārito nāradena tat-sutau mṛtyum ātmanaḥ' (his senses agitated with anger; those two sons were his death, though Narada restrained him).

statements.claim: Kamsa seized his sword, had Vasudeva taken, bound Devaki beside her husband, and put both back into iron fetters.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.15-18 (rendered): 'hearing this, Kamsa seized his sword and bound Vasudeva and Devaki in iron fetters.'

statements.claim: Kamsa's killings of Devaki's infants had all been for nothing, because the one child that mattered had been slipped out beneath his hand.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83 (DKS_0128 pack): 'I perpetrated a dreadful and highly censurable deed and destroyed the six heroic sons of Devaki'; the transference story (VP 5.15) shows the eighth child escaped that fate.

notes: Tracks SB 10.36.15-18 and VP 5.15. 'Dashed against a stone' and 'across the Yamuna' are canonical details of the transference account the pack references — treated as supported. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa went to the arena himself to look over the ground, a hall built by skilled hands: courtyard ringed with pillars of even size, turrets with pleasant rooms, raised royal seats, passages for a great crowd, walls hung with strong tusks of elephants.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'the king went to the arena for examining the platforms. This hall was constructed by clever artizans... turrets consisting of beautiful rooms. It had a spacious courtyard and a number of pillars of the same size. It was bedecked on all sides with strong tusks of elephants and with spacious, high and royal seats. It had many passages.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the platforms and turrets hung with garlands, flags and sweet scents, golden jars of water set out in order, and the bow festival announced for the fourteenth day of the month.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Let the platforms, turrets and passages be embellished with garlands, flags and covers and be sweet-scented... Let excellent golden jars full of water be placed in due order'; SB 10.36.25: 'ārabhyatāṃ dhanur-yāgaś caturdaśyāṃ yathā-vidhi' (let the bow sacrifice be begun on the fourteenth, according to rite).

statements.claim: Kamsa sent for his wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika, the two strongest men in Mathura, whose lives had been shaped by his favor.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Kansa sent for Chānura and Mushthika the two wrestlers of unequalled strength... You are both my heroic wrestlers well-known (in the world)... the honors I have showered upon you.'

statements.claim: Kamsa told them they would face the two cowherd boys from Vraja, Krishna and Balarama, and ordered them thrown to the ground and killed, warning them not to dismiss the boys as of fickle nature, since these two had been shown to him as his death.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'fighting in the arena with those two forest-ranging cow-herd boys Krishna and Sangkarshana who have grown in Vraja for me you will be able to throw them on earth and kill them... do not disregard them as boys of fickle nature'; SB 10.36.22: 'rāma-kṛṣṇau tato mahyaṃ mṛtyuḥ kila nidarśitaḥ' (these two have been shown to me as my death).

statements.claim: If the boys fell in the ring, Kamsa's well-being would be secure now and in the time to come.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'If those two boys are killed in battle in the arena I shall meet with well-being both in present and future.'

statements.claim: The wrestlers promised: if the two helpless boys come before them, count them already slain; if they withstand them, they will destroy them in the king's very presence.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'If those two helpless boys... come before us know them as already slain... if those two forest-rangers... withstand us, we will destroy them in your very presence.'

statements.claim: Kamsa told his elephant-master Mahamatra to keep the elephant Kuvalayapida at the gate of the arena — temples running with rut, eyes never sober, always in a fury against men — and drive it at the sons of Vasudeva so they would be deprived of their lives before reaching the ring.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.83: 'Kansa said to his elephant-trainer Mahāmātra: Keep at the gate of the arena... the elephant Kuvalayapida... whose temples are soaked with temporal juice, eyes are always inebriate and who is always angry with men. When the mean forest-ranging sons of Vasudeva will come do you so drive that elephant at them that they might at once be deprived of their lives.'

statements.claim: Kamsa would not go to Vraja himself nor fight Krishna with his own hands, but would let the elephant and the wrestlers do it before the city's eyes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.26: Kamsa sends the foremost of the Yadus (Akrura) to fetch the boys (DKS_0129 pack); Harivamsha 1.83: killing through wrestlers or elephant; consistent with Kamsa's plan to destroy the boys 'whilst they were yet young' (VP 5.15).

notes: Tracks Harivamsha 1.83 and SB 10.36.19-26. 'Fourteenth day of the month' follows SB (caturdaśyām); Harivamsha says 'tomorrow' — sources differ, story follows the SB rendering. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: Kamsa sent for Akrura, foremost among the Yadavas, called the lord of gifts for his generosity.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.26-27: 'āhūya yadu-puṅgavam' (summoning the foremost of the Yadus); 'bho bho dāna-pate' (O lord of gifts); VP 5.15: 'the noble Yadu, Akrúra the son of Swaphalka... Lord of liberal gifts'.

statements.claim: Kamsa took Akrura by the hand and spoke warmly, asking him to go to Vraja, to Nanda's settlement, and bring back the two boys, Krishna and Balarama, for the bow festival.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Kamsa, taking Akrura by the hand, sent him with sweet words to bring Krishna and Balarama from Vraja, saying the bow sacrifice was to be seen'; SB 10.36.29: 'gaccha nanda-vrajaṃ tatra sutāv ānakadundubheḥ' (go to Nanda's Vraja; there the two sons of Vasudeva).

statements.claim: Kamsa revealed that the two boys were the means by which the gods had appointed his death, and that when brought he would have them killed by the elephant, like one slain by death itself.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.30-31: 'nisṛṣṭaḥ kila me mṛtyur devair vaikuṇṭha-saṃśrayaiḥ... ghātayiṣya ihānītau kāla-kalpena hastinā' (my death appointed by the gods; I will have them killed by the elephant like time/death itself).

statements.claim: When the two were dead, the earth would be free of its thorns at last.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.34: 'tataś caiṣā mahī mitra bhavitrī naṣṭa-kaṇṭakā' (then this earth, friend, will be free of thorns).

statements.claim: Kamsa named the allies who had thrown in their lot with him, trusting Akrura as his own right hand.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.35: 'śambaro narako bāṇo mayy eva kṛta-sauhṛdāḥ' (Shambara, Naraka and Bana have made friendship with me); SB 10.36.27: 'kriyatāṃ maitram ādṛtaḥ' (do me this friendship, honored).

statements.claim: Akrura was not deceived: he knew Kamsa's intent — that the boys were not meant to return — yet he agreed to go.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36 (rendered): 'Akrura, though he knew Kamsa's intent, agreed to carry out the command.'

statements.claim: Akrura's answer, as recorded in the verses: even men whose hopes have been struck down by fate go on entertaining their hopes.
statements.evidence: SB 10.36.38: 'manorathān karoty uccair jano daiva-hatān api' (people entertain their hopes high even when struck down by fate).

notes: Tracks SB 10.36.26-39 with Harivamsha 1.77 / VP 5.15 corroboration. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.

statements.claim: In the afternoon Krishna and Balarama entered Mathura with the cowherds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.18, 23: 'athāparāhne bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ' (in the afternoon the blessed Krishna with Samkarshana); 'tāṃ sampraviṣṭau vasudeva-nandanau vṛtau vayasyair naradeva-vartmanā' (the two sons of Vasudeva entered, surrounded by companions, along the kings' road).

statements.claim: The city rose before them dressed for a festival: a gateway of crystal with doors of gold and golden arches, crossroads of gold, high mansions and terraced gardens, rows of houses and open assembly halls, doves and peacocks calling in the lattice windows.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.19-21: 'sphāṭika-tuṇga-gopura-dvārāṃ bṛhad-dhema-kapāṭa-toraṇām... sauvarṇa-śṛṅgāṭaka-harmya-niṣkuṭaiḥ śreṇī-sabhābhir bhavanair upaskṛtām... āviṣṭa-pārāvata-barhi-nāditām'.

statements.claim: Water pots stood full along the streets; the ground was sprinkled with curd and sandalwood; garlands of flowers and strings of lamps hung among fresh green leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.22: 'āpūrṇa-kumbhair dadhi-candanokṣitaiḥ prasūna-dīpāvalibhiḥ sa-pallavaiḥ' (full water-pots, sprinkled with curd and sandalwood, garlands of flowers and rows of lamps with fresh leaves).

statements.claim: The women of the city came running; in their haste one dressed with clothes and ornaments inside out, another forgot one of a pair (a single earring, a single anklet), another lined only one eye with kajal, some set down their food halfway, some left off being rubbed with oil before the bath was done.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.24-25: 'viparyag-dhṛta-vastra-bhūṣaṇā... vismṛtya caikaṃ yugaleṣv... kṛtaika-patra-śravanaika-nūpurā... nāṅktvā dvitīyaṃ... locanam... aśnantya ekās tad apāsya... abhyajyamānā akṛtopamajjanāḥ'.

statements.claim: The lotus-eyed Krishna's bold, easy smiles and teasing glances were like nectar poured out; the women drank the sight of him and embraced his form with their eyes, their skin thrilling, their long-carried sorrow loosening and falling away.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.26-27: 'manāṃsi tāsām aravinda-locanaḥ pragalbha-līlā-hasitāvalokaiḥ... tat-prekṣaṇotsmita-sudhokṣaṇa-labdha-mānāḥ... ānanda-mūrtim upaguhya dṛśātma-labdhaṃ hṛṣyat-tvaco jahur anantam arindamādhim' (lotus-eyed, bold playful smiles and glances; nectar-sprinkling; embracing the blissful form with their eyes; skin thrilling; they gave up their endless sorrow).

statements.claim: Those who could not reach the street climbed to the rooftops and showered down curd and unbroken rice and water, garlands and sweet scents, like offerings.
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.28-29: 'prāsāda-śikharārūḍhāḥ prīty-utphulla-mukhāmbujāḥ... dadhy-akṣataiḥ soda-pātraiḥ srag-gandhair abhyupāyanaiḥ' (climbing to palace tops, faces blossoming with joy; curd, unbroken rice, water-pots, garlands, scents as offerings). The 'could not reach the street' motive is connective.

statements.claim: The people of the city called out in wonder: what great austerities must these gopis have performed, that they can see him whenever they wish?
statements.evidence: SB 10.41.30: 'ūcuḥ paurā aho gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran mahat' (the citizens said: aho, what great austerities did these gopis perform).

notes: Tracks SB 10.41.18-30 closely, following the Sanskrit passage (citizens/paurāḥ shower offerings) rather than the pack's rendered note mentioning brahmins — story matches the authoritative passage. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims.
